text:
anya: quick heads-up — ran a smoke onboarding of nova-v1 int8 against the multilingual dev bundle and noticed a reproducible issue: U+202F (narrow no-break space) between CJK and latin is being dropped in outputs, causing token join and ~0.9 BLEU loss on zh->en subset.

kai: repro'd locally, small repro below. input -> model output (int8) shows join, fp16 baseline preserves the narrowspace.
```
# repro snippet
echo -n "中国
202Fmix test: 这是 a test." | ./run_infer --model nova-v1 --quant int8 --input -
# output-int8: 中国mix test: 这是a test.
# output-fp16: 中国
202Fmix test: 这是 a test.
```

sanjay: hmm. is the tokenizer normalizing U+202F to nothing or merging it into previous token pre-tokenization? can you paste the token ids for both runs?

kai: token ids: int8 run and fp16 run produce same tokenization pre-inference when I tokenize locally with our tokenizer binary. So appears post-tokenization transformation (serving/runtime) — either detokenization path or generation detok step.

marie: checked the console traces for that job. The response detok path goes through `detok-service:v2` in private deploy. There's a path where we run `normalize_whitespace()` with `collapse_narrow_spaces=true` on older detok build. Might be that the private deployment image used for int8 onboarding has that flag enabled.

hao: I grabbed the exact container image from the int8 canary: `redwood/detok:2024-11-int8-canary`. That image still has legacy whitespace patch. Newer detok (main) has `preserve_u202f=true` by default.

anya: oh interesting — does that align with the timing of the quant bring-up? The int8 canary uses the older detok image because of pinned deps (we pinned for OS-level libs).

eng-runtime-bot: [deploy] job nova-v1-int8-canary -> started on host gpu-canary-03 :rocket:

kai: quick experiment — I re-ran the int8 inference but bypassed the detok-service (raw tokens -> join with simple joiner). Output preserved the narrowspace. That suggests the problem is detok-side.

marie: agrees. I also pulled the server logs: `detok-service` applied `unicode_collapse(normalize=True)` which maps U+202F to zero-width no-break in that old branch. There's a unit test missing for mixed CJK-latin narrowspace.

sanjay: ok so at least it's not a quant kernel bug. But we should still check if quant rollout workflows implicitly pin to that detok image (so int8 customers see this).

anya: plan: (1) open a quick PR to detok to revert collapse behavior, add a unit test for U+202F mixing; (2) patch the int8 canary config to point at `detok:main` for postprocess; (3) re-run the smoke suite and post BLEU/WER diff.

hao: I'll prepare the PR and add that unit test. tagging @eng-runtime since detok image pinning is in the deployment manifest.

marie: adding a guard in the bring-up checklist: verify detok image in canary matches main if you're toggling whitespace-sensitive locales.

kai: re-run after swapping detok to main — BLEU delta goes back to baseline (0.02). Verified on the same dev shard.

ci-bot: [CI] build detok PR #458 passed \u2014 12 tests, 1 flake skipped :white_check_mark:

anya: nice. follow-ups: (a) note in the onboarding doc that int8 brings up can pull older dep images; (b) add a quick locale smoke for zh/en that includes narrow/no-break spaces in CI to catch regressions; (c) we should check similar behavior for U+2009 (thin space) and U+00A0 (NBSP).

sanjay: also recommend a short integration test in `infra/serving/manifest-tests` that verifies `detok-version` >= main commit hash for any quant canary. Keeps pin drift from biting us.

anya: thanks all — great triage. marking as resolved for now, will reopen if we find other narrowspace variants failing. :thumbsup:
